nodes.name: Theorem 1
Theorem 2
Theorem 6
nodes.statement:
Let Assumptions 1 and 2 be true, and let $\beta(f):=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^ny_i^{\top}\theta^*-\left<\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}= \overline{Y\theta^*} - \left<\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}$ be the minimizing $\beta\in I_\tau$ for fixed $f\in \mathcal{H}_{\tau}$ in the modified empirical risk. There exists constants $C_1,C_2>0$ such that for all $\varepsilon>0$
\[
\mathbb{P}\Big(\sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau} |R_{\text{emp}}(f)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta(f))|>\varepsilon \Big)\leq C_1 \exp\Big( -\frac{C_2n \varepsilon^2}{1+(\kappa\tau)^2}\Big).
\]

nodes.name: Theorem 3
nodes.statement:
Under Assumptions 1-3, there exists a constant $C_2 > 0$ such that for all $\varepsilon>0$, 
$$
\mathbb{P}\Big(\sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau\,,\, \beta\in I_\tau}\{R(f,\beta)-\widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta)\}>\varepsilon\Big)
\leq  2\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}\exp\Big(-  \frac{n\varepsilon^2}{128(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{4}}\Big),
$$
where $\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}=\{1+2(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa\tau)/\varepsilon\} 
\exp( C_2\tau^2 \varepsilon^{-2})$.

nodes.name: Theorem 4
nodes.statement:
Let $\widehat{\beta}=-\left<\,\overline{\Phi}, \widehat{f}\,\right>_{\mathcal{H}}$. Under Assumptions 1 and 2, there exist constants $C_1, C_2>0$ such that for all $\varepsilon>0,$
 \[
\mathbb{P}\Big(\Big| \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})\Big|>\varepsilon\Big) \leq C_1\exp\Big( -\frac{C_2n \varepsilon^2}{1+(\kappa\tau)^2}\Big).
 \]

nodes.name: Theorem 5
nodes.statement:
Under Assumptions 1 and 2, for all $\varepsilon>0$
$$
\mathbb{P}\Big(\widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde f, \widetilde \beta)-R(f^\ast, \beta^\ast) >\varepsilon \Big)
\leq 2\exp\Big( -\frac{n\varepsilon^2}{16(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa\tau)^{4}}\Big).
$$

nodes.name: Lemma 5
Lemma 4
Lemma 7
nodes.statement: Let Assumption 1 be true. For all $\varepsilon>0$, we have $\mathbb{P}\big((\overline{Y\theta^*})^2>\varepsilon \big)\leq  2 \exp(- n \varepsilon/\|\theta^*\|_\infty)$.

nodes.name: Lemma 6
nodes.statement:
Under Assumption 1 there exist constants $C_1, C_2>0$ such that for all $\varepsilon>0$,
$$
\mathbb{P}\bigg(\max\Big(|n_1/n_2-\pi_1/\pi_2|,|n_2/n_1-\pi_2/\pi_1|\Big)>\varepsilon\bigg)\leq C_1 \exp\Big(- C_2 n \varepsilon^2 \Big),
$$
$$
\mathbb{P}\bigg(\max\Big(|\sqrt{n_1/n_2}-\sqrt{\pi_1/\pi_2}|,|\sqrt{n_2/n_1}-\sqrt{\pi_2/\pi_1}|\Big)>\varepsilon\bigg)\leq C_1 \exp\Big(- C_2 n \varepsilon^2 \Big).
$$

nodes.name: Lemma 10
Lemma 9
nodes.statement: Let $\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{2n}$ be the data, and consider an $L^{2}(T_x)$ $\varepsilon$-net $\{f_1, \dots, f_M\}$ of $\mathcal{H}_\tau$. Then $\{f_1, \dots, f_M\}$ is an $\sqrt{2}\varepsilon$-net with respect to the empirical measure on half of the data $\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{n}$.
